title: Move a Windows DNS Zone to Azure DNS

cta.text: See Micetro with your Microsoft and Azure DNS

prompt:
Product: BlueCat. Demo: "Move a Windows DNS Zone to Azure DNS".
Start with one welcome step whose title is exactly "Copy a Windows DNS Zone to Azure DNS in One Dialog" and whose text is exactly: Watch BlueCat Micetro copy a zone and all its records from a Windows DNS server to Azure DNS, while the original stays in place until you choose to retire it.
Audience: network and DNS engineers and IT leaders evaluating the product. Tone: concise, confident, practical, no hype.
12 screenshots, keep this order, one tooltip per image, calling out the highlighted UI element. Use the text of each numbered tooltip EXACTLY as written; do not rewrite, shorten or merge it. Do not add a closing step or a closing message after the last screenshot; its own tooltip is the end.
1. This is the DNS page in Micetro. Every zone from every DNS server it manages is in one list: Windows servers, BIND, AWS and Azure. The Authority column says where each zone lives. Filter the list to find one.
2. One zone, cloudapps.ddi-legal.net, hosted on a Windows DNS server (DLG-DC01). Point at its row and the ellipsis button appears: that opens the row menu.
3. The row menu holds everything you can do to a zone. First, look inside it: choose Open zone.
4. Four hosts and two aliases. This is what has to arrive in Azure intact. Select Back to list.
5. Back at the zone, open the row menu again. This time choose Migrate zone.
6. Migrate zone asks one question: where should the zone go? The list holds every platform Micetro manages, including each Azure resource group. Without Micetro this is a zone export from Windows, a private zone created in Azure, an import and a check of the records. Here it is one dialog. Pick the DDItoday resource group.
7. Remove original zone stays clear, so this makes a copy. The Windows zone keeps answering until you decide to retire it. Select Migrate.
8. Micetro asks for a reason on every change, and keeps it in the zone's history. Add a short comment, then save.
9. Migrated. The zone and its records were created in Azure. Close the result.
10. The zone now exists twice. The first row is the new copy: the side panel shows its Authority is the Azure subscription and its View is the DDItoday resource group. The Windows copy is still there.
11. Open the Azure copy the same way as before.
12. The same four hosts and two aliases are now served from Azure. Retire the Windows copy whenever you choose.
